title: RAP-RNA
method_names: RAP-RNA (Engreitz et al., 2014 RNA–RNA interaction mapping)
scope: Illumina explanatory schematic of RNA sequencing from RAP isolates containing biotinylated antisense RNA capture probes, ending at an adapter-flanked amplified cDNA library. The 2013 primary paper names the enrichment method RNA Antisense Purification (RAP) and supports sequencing recovered RNA as well as a separate DNA readout. The 2014 abstract explicitly names an RNA–RNA interaction-mapping method RAP-RNA; its detailed probe/library chemistry is not established here, so the two uses of the label are qualified rather than treated as identical implementations.

operations.label: Wash-off probes with streptavidin
operations.description: Separates biotinylated probe RNA with its still-annealed cDNA onto streptavidin; retains the endogenous RNA-derived cDNA fraction for library completion. The depicted removal is a selection rather than a new cDNA synthesis step.
operations.mechanism: Biotin on probe RNA provides the streptavidin affinity handle; RNA–cDNA annealing links the probe-derived cDNA to that handle.
operations.information_effect: Reduces capture-probe sequence contamination. Survival of this selection does not prove that every retained cellular RNA specifically or directly interacts with the target.

method_scopes.rationale: All six operations apply to the displayed RNA-probe-containing RAP isolate route, with o_rap summarizing initial purification context. Illumina calls this RAP-RNA. The 2013 paper names its capture method RAP and verifies RNA enrichment/sequencing, but its inspected main methods emphasize chromatin/DNA isolation and do not independently establish the depicted RNA-library details. Its Figure 1D DNA readout is separate from the DNase-treated cDNA route here.

method_scopes.method: RAP-RNA (Engreitz et al., 2014 RNA–RNA interaction mapping)
method_scopes.rationale: The supplied 2014 abstract explicitly describes RAP-RNA as RNA–RNA interaction mapping with differential crosslinking: direct hybridization for U1 and indirect protein-mediated associations for Malat1. This supports a related, explicitly named assay scope. It does not establish applicability of the displayed RNA-probe library and streptavidin-depletion operations; no internal workflow is assigned from an abstract alone.

evidence.quote: To identify these contacts, we developed a method based on RNA antisense purification to systematically map RNA-RNA interactions (RAP-RNA)

Using differential crosslinking, we confirmed that U1 directly hybridizes to 5' splice sites and 5' splice site motifs throughout introns and found that Malat1 interacts with pre-mRNAs indirectly through protein intermediates.
evidence.rationale: This establishes distinct biological association classes in the separately described RAP-RNA RNA–RNA mapping method; it supplies no library-preparation order.

unknowns.question: The drawing places the first red adapter at the same left side previously labeled 5′P. Which RNA terminus actually receives this adapter? Neither the supplied card nor the inspected 2013 main text states the polarity. The supplementary RNA-library method or a corrected end-labeled figure is needed to assign it. This limits end-specific chemistry, not the depicted dephosphorylation → adapter addition → reverse-transcription order.

Does the 2014 RAP-RNA RNA–RNA interaction implementation use these RNA capture probes and post-RT streptavidin depletion? Its supplied abstract does not specify the relevant probe and library chemistry; the full methods would resolve this applicability.
